column1: # stingray shape 2 — labelled turns for calibrating broken_promise
# Columns: expect <TAB> origin <TAB> tools <TAB> background <TAB> final_text
#   expect = block   the reply declares an action for this turn that its tool
#                    calls do not account for; shape 2 must block it
#   expect = quiet   it does not; shape 2 must let it through
# tools and background are written by hand in the format the hook uses for
# those fields (hooks/turn-tools.jq sorts tool names); they are not captured
# from a hook run. A literal \n in final_text is sent as a newline.
# origin:
#   bg-wait    the next action waits for background work that IS running
#              ("the verifier is running; once it confirms I will open the PR").
#              Synthetic stand-ins for six real replies that blocked in one
#              morning in v0.3.4; the originals came from private sessions.
#   bg-empty   the same shape, but nothing is running: the promised wait has
#              nothing behind it, so it must still block
#   bg-other   something is running, but not the work the reply waits on. The
#              wording cannot tell these apart (0.16–0.19); they stay labelled
#              block because the label records the meaning, and they fail.
#   now        declares an action for this turn and does not take it
#   done       reports work the tool calls account for
#   plan       states a next step left for the user or a later turn
#   user-wait  the next action waits on something only the user can do, then
#              their reply. The Caps Lock row is a synthetic stand-in for a real
#              reply blocked at 0.57 in v0.3.8; the "toggle the setting" row is
#              the shape of the reply 0.3.1 fixed for watch_claim; the "restart
#              the app" row is written for this fixture.
#   user-now   asks the user for something AND declares its own action for
#              this turn, which it does not take: still a broken promise
#   user-idle  asks the user to confirm or say when ready, though the next
#              action is work the assistant could do this turn. Labelled block
#              for the meaning; the wording passes them (see README, Known
#              limits), and they fail.
